raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Summary

Size HybridEngine rollout KV caches from each rank's own prefill KV tensors, not from the global model config. Under AutoTP, each rank holds only its share of the KV heads. Today the cache is allocated for the full model's KV-head count, so TP>1 rollout fails on all three decode paths:

| Path | TP>1 failure today | Change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Plain graph (`_generate_graph`) | Passing batch size, device and dtype makes `DeepSpeedStaticCache` initialize from `module.config` up front, so the lazy per-layer setup never runs. The prefill copy then fails with `4 vs 2` heads, or broadcasts silently when the rank has 1 local head. | Drop those up-front arguments, so the existing lazy setup sizes each layer from the prefill tensors before capture. |
| Continuous eager (`_generate_continuous`) | The same up-front setup from config fails on the first prefill copy (`4 vs 2`, `2 vs 8`). | Create the cache lazily. `_continuous_cache_layer` initializes each layer from the prefill tensors, sized to the slot count. The slot count is the decode batch capacity, not the prefill batch. |
| Continuous graph | The graph state cache is initialized from config, and capture happens before any prefill. | Create the cache lazily and run one decode forward on the current stream before warmup, so every layer is initialized with local shapes. Without this, those tensors would be allocated on the warmup side stream. |

`lazy_initialization` gains an optional `max_batch_size`, which the continuous path uses because its capacity is the slot count. `cache_memory_bytes` is now computed after decode, once the layers exist. No model config is changed and no TP/world group is consulted, so TP×DP layouts work with no extra logic.

## Related work / scope

- #9000 / #9004 fix attention-mask construction during capture, not KV shape allocation. This PR is independent of them. For real Hugging Face model validation, #9004's runtime hunk was applied to **both** the baseline and the fixed tree.
- #8602 divides cache heads by the global world size, which breaks TP×DP (for example TP2×DP4). This fix reads the tensors directly instead of inferring the TP group.
- On Transformers 5.17, continuous eager also needs #8852 (`get_query_offset`), which is still open, so the continuous eager HF runs below apply #8852 to both baseline and fixed trees. The new unit tests use a local model and do not depend on #8852.
- **Known limitation, not changed here:** a persistent continuous graph (#8732) that contains NCCL ops makes `torch.distributed.destroy_process_group()` hang in `ProcessGroupNCCL.shutdown()` at exit. Releasing the rollout (`del` + `gc.collect()` + `synchronize()`) before destroying avoids it. Before this PR, TP>1 continuous graph could not run, so the hang was not reachable. A release/close API is left for a follow-up.

## Validation

**Hardware/software:** 8× NVIDIA L20, driver 580.173.02, CUDA runtime 13.0, torch 2.14.1+cu130, Transformers 5.17.0, Python 3.10.22. Baseline: `d8241a9ba266405e1a58fadf19e24b2370f6d7fa`.

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python -m pytest --forked tests/unit/v1/test_hybrid_engine_rollout_v1.py \
  -k "static_graph_uses_prefill_kv_shape or continuous_generation_uses_local_kv_shape"
# baseline: 6 failed, 3 passed; this PR: 9 passed

CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python -m pytest --forked tests/unit/v1/test_hybrid_engine_rollout_v1.py \
  tests/unit/runtime/rollout/test_hybrid_engine_rollout.py tests/unit/utils/test_static_cache.py
# baseline: 6 failed, 64 passed, 1 skipped; this PR: 70 passed, 1 skipped
```

The new tests write head-dependent cache contents, compare tokens with an independent oracle, and count real graph replays:

| Local / config KV heads | Plain graph | Continuous eager | Continuous graph |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 4 / 4 | pass → pass | pass → pass | pass → pass |
| 2 / 4 | fail → pass | fail → pass | fail → pass |
| 1 / 4 | fail → pass | fail → pass | fail → pass |

**Multi-GPU tiny Llama, continuous path.** 2 layers, 4 KV heads, fp32, 4 requests per rank, 2 slots. Tokens were compared with plain eager generation on every rank.

| Layout | Continuous graph (before → after) | Continuous eager + #8852 (before → after) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TP1, world 1 | pass → pass | pass → pass |
| TP2, world 2 | shape error → pass | `4 vs 2` error → pass |
| TP4, world 4 | shape error → pass | `2 vs 8` error → pass |
| TP2×DP4, world 8 | shape error → pass | `4 vs 2` error → pass |
| TP4×DP2, world 8 | not run → pass | `2 vs 8` error → pass |

**Plain graph with real models**, with #9004 applied to both trees:

| Model / precision | Layouts | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tiny Llama / fp32 | TP1×DP1, TP1×DP4, TP2×DP2, TP2×DP4 | All pass; graph tokens and masks equal native eager generation |
| Qwen3-8B / bf16 | TP2×DP4 | 4 prompts × 16 new tokens; graph tokens and masks equal native eager generation |

On the plain-graph runs, each rank made three generation calls: 3 captures and 45 replays, and repeated graph outputs matched. The baseline TP2×DP4 Llama run failed at the KV copy (`4 vs 2`). The Qwen3 graph calls took 0.464 / 0.439 s, including prefill and capture, with 8.25 GiB max allocated per GPU. These numbers come from correctness runs; **no speedup is claimed**.

**Distributed AutoTP integration test** (`TestAutoTPContinuousRollout`, world size 2): real AutoTP via `deepspeed.initialize` (`autotp_size=2`) on a tiny Llama, 3 requests on 2 continuous slots, tokens compared with `generate()` on the same sharded model. On 2× NVIDIA H20, torch 2.9.0a0+50eac811a6.nv25.09, Transformers 4.57.6, Python 3.12.3:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 python -m pytest tests/unit/v1/test_hybrid_engine_rollout_v1.py -k TestAutoTPContinuousRollout
# baseline (rollout + static cache from d8241a9): 2 failed (eager `4 vs 2`, graph `[2, 2, 16]` vs `[2, 4, 16]`); this PR: 2 passed
```

```bash
DS_ACCELERATOR=cpu python -m pytest tests/unit/runtime/rollout/test_hybrid_engine_rollout.py \
  tests/unit/utils/test_static_cache.py tests/unit/v1/test_hybrid_engine_rollout_v1.py
# 60 passed, 11 skipped; Python 3.12.3 / torch 2.14.0.dev20260804+xpu

pre-commit run --files deepspeed/runtime/rollout/hybrid_engine_rollout.py \
  deepspeed/utils/static_cache.py tests/unit/v1/test_hybrid_engine_rollout_v1.py
# passed
```

**Intel XPU** (1× Arc Pro B70, torch 2.14.1+xpu, Transformers 5.22.1, Intel compute runtime 26.27.39122.11, Level Zero loader 1.28.2). Master has no XPU graph backend, so the new graph tests skip there. On top of #9007 (XPU graph capture):

```bash
DS_ACCELERATOR=xpu python -m pytest tests/unit/v1/test_hybrid_engine_rollout_v1.py \
  -k "static_graph_uses_prefill_kv_shape or continuous_generation_uses_local_kv_shape"
# #9007 alone: 6 failed, 3 passed; #9007 + this PR: 9 passed

DS_ACCELERATOR=xpu python -m pytest tests/unit/v1/test_hybrid_engine_rollout_v1.py \
  tests/unit/runtime/rollout/test_hybrid_engine_rollout.py
# #9007 + this PR: 60 passed, 3 skipped; process exit 0
```

This clean-exit torch 2.14.1 rerun confirms all nine new tests pass; the same tests against #9007 without this PR give 6 failed / 3 passed (exit 1). The earlier torch 2.15.0+xpu run printed passing tests but aborts during interpreter teardown on this host (exit 134). A minimal XPU tensor program reproduces that abort without DeepSpeed, so that earlier run is not counted as a clean test pass. The earlier master-based tree reported 52 passed / 10 skipped, with graph coverage skipped as expected.

The opt-in `test_continuous_graph_matches_pretrained_model_when_enabled` (only runs when `DEEPSPEED_PRETRAINED_ROLLOUT_MODEL` is set) fails the same way on master and on this PR with Transformers 5.17: `'DeepSpeedStaticCache' object has no attribute 'get_query_offset'`, which #8852 addresses.

**Validated:** ZeRO-0, no offload, fp32/bf16, AutoTP with data-parallel replicas on CUDA, plain and continuous decode, eager and graph; single-device graph tests on XPU with #9007. **Not validated:** a full training-to-rollout cycle, ZeRO-1/2/3, offload, pipeline/expert/sequence parallelism, older HF preallocated cache APIs, and multi-device XPU graph. No claim is made about training convergence or performance.

AI assistance: GitHub Copilot helped with the implementation, the tests and the validation. I reviewed every changed line before signing off.

Added in 766d560: `TestAutoTPContinuousRollout` (`world_size = 2`) in `tests/unit/v1/test_hybrid_engine_rollout_v1.py`. It runs real AutoTP through `deepspeed.initialize` with `tensor_parallel.autotp_size=2` on a tiny Llama (4 KV heads, so each rank holds 2), and checks that the `k_proj` shards are actually split. It then runs continuous rollout with 3 requests on 2 slots, so a refill lands in an already allocated cache row. The tokens must equal `generate()` on the same sharded model, for both eager and graph capture.

Results on 2× NVIDIA H20, torch 2.9.0a0+50eac811a6.nv25.09, Transformers 4.57.6, Python 3.12.3:

| Tree | eager | graph |
| --- | --- | --- |
| this PR | pass | pass |
| rollout + static cache reverted to d8241a9 | `size of tensor a (4) must match ... b (2)` | `value tensor of shape [2, 2, 16] cannot be broadcast to ... [2, 4, 16]` |

Plain graph is not in this test, because real HF models need the mask fix in #9004 for that path; the TP2/TP2×DP4 plain-graph runs with #9004 are reported in the description. On Transformers versions whose `Cache` defines `get_query_offset` (5.x), the eager case skips until #8852 lands. The graph case still runs there. The test releases the rollout before process-group teardown because of the known NCCL graph teardown hang noted in the description.

+import gc

 import torch
 from transformers import PretrainedConfig

+import deepspeed
 from deepspeed.accelerator import get_accelerator
 from deepspeed.runtime.rollout.base import RolloutRequest, SamplingConfig
 from deepspeed.runtime.rollout.hybrid_engine_rollout import HybridEngineRollout, HybridEngineRolloutConfig
+from deepspeed.utils.static_cache import DeepSpeedStaticCache
+from unit.common import DistributedTest

+class _LocalKVModel(torch.nn.Module):
+    """Emits fewer KV heads than its global config, like an AutoTP shard."""
+    _supports_cache_class = True
+
+    def __init__(self, local_heads):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.local_heads = local_heads
+        self.weight = torch.nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(1))
+        self.config = PretrainedConfig(max_position_embeddings=32,
+                                       num_hidden_layers=1,
+                                       num_attention_heads=4,
+                                       num_key_value_heads=4,
+                                       hidden_size=4,
+                                       head_dim=1)
+
+    def forward(self, input_ids, attention_mask, past_key_values=None, cache_position=None, **kwargs):
+        heads = torch.arange(1, self.local_heads + 1, device=input_ids.device)
+        states = input_ids[:, None, :, None].float() * heads[None, :, None, None]
+        _, values = past_key_values.update(states,
+                                           states,
+                                           layer_idx=0,
+                                           cache_kwargs={"cache_position": cache_position})
+        if attention_mask.dim() == 4:
+            valid = attention_mask[:, 0, 0, :] == 0
+        else:
+            valid = torch.zeros((values.shape[0], values.shape[2]), dtype=torch.bool, device=input_ids.device)
+            valid[:, :attention_mask.shape[1]] = attention_mask.bool()
+        cache_sums = (values * valid[:, None, :, None]).sum(dim=(1, 2, 3)).long()
+        next_tokens = cache_sums.remainder(29) + 3
+        logits = torch.zeros((input_ids.shape[0], input_ids.shape[1], 32), device=input_ids.device)
+        logits.scatter_(2, next_tokens[:, None, None].expand(-1, input_ids.shape[1], 1), 1)
+        return SimpleNamespace(logits=logits)
+
+
+def _local_kv_tokens(prompts, new_tokens, local_heads):
+    head_sum = sum(range(1, local_heads + 1))
+    expected = []
+    for prompt in prompts:
+        tokens = list(prompt)
+        for _ in range(new_tokens):
+            tokens.append(sum(tokens) * head_sum % 29 + 3)
+        expected.append(tokens)
+    return expected
+
+
+def _count_replays(monkeypatch, accelerator):
+    counter = {"replays": 0}
+    original_replay = accelerator.replay_graph
+
+    def replay(graph):
+        counter["replays"] += 1
+        return original_replay(graph)
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(accelerator, "replay_graph", replay)
+    return counter

+    if not accelerator.is_available() or accelerator.create_graph() is None:

+    model = _LocalKVModel(local_heads).to(device).eval()
+    rollout = HybridEngineRollout(SimpleNamespace(module=model),

+                                  cfg=HybridEngineRolloutConfig(use_graph_capture=True))
+    prompts = [[1, 3, 4], [3, 4, 5]]
+    prompt_ids = torch.tensor(prompts, device=device)
+    new_tokens = 4
+    output = rollout.generate(RolloutRequest(prompt_ids, torch.ones_like(prompt_ids)),
+                              SamplingConfig(max_new_tokens=new_tokens, temperature=0))
+
+    assert output.input_ids.tolist() == _local_kv_tokens(prompts, new_tokens, local_heads)
+    assert counter["replays"] == new_tokens - 1
+    assert model.config.num_key_value_heads == 4
+

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("use_graph", [False, True])

+    accelerator = get_accelerator()
+    if use_graph and (not accelerator.is_available() or accelerator.create_graph() is None):
+        pytest.skip("requires graph capture")

+    counter = _count_replays(monkeypatch, accelerator)
+    device = torch.device(accelerator.device_name())
+    model = _LocalKVModel(local_heads).to(device).eval()
+    rollout = HybridEngineRollout(SimpleNamespace(module=model),
+                                  SimpleNamespace(pad_token_id=0, eos_token_id=-1),
+                                  cfg=HybridEngineRolloutConfig(use_graph_capture=use_graph))
+    # Three requests on two slots force a refill into an already allocated cache row.
+    prompts = [[1, 3, 4], [3, 4, 5], [2, 2, 6]]
+    prompt_ids = torch.tensor(prompts, device=device)
+    new_tokens = 4
+    output = rollout.generate(RolloutRequest(prompt_ids, torch.ones_like(prompt_ids)),
+                              SamplingConfig(max_new_tokens=new_tokens, temperature=0, continuous_batch_size=2))

+    assert output.input_ids.tolist() == _local_kv_tokens(prompts, new_tokens, local_heads)
+    decode_steps = rollout.get_last_continuous_stats()["decode_steps"]
+    assert counter["replays"] == (decode_steps if use_graph else 0)
+    assert decode_steps > 0

+    world_size = 2

+            pytest.skip("requires graph capture")
+        # Eager continuous decode passes a 2-D mask, so newer Transformers query the cache offset.

+        cache_has_offset = hasattr(DeepSpeedStaticCache, "get_query_offset")
+        if not use_graph and hf_needs_offset and not cache_has_offset:
+            pytest.skip("DeepSpeedStaticCache lacks get_query_offset for this Transformers version")
+
+        from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, LlamaConfig
+
+        config = LlamaConfig(vocab_size=128,
+                             hidden_size=64,
+                             intermediate_size=128,
+                             num_hidden_layers=2,
+                             num_attention_heads=4,
+                             num_key_value_heads=4,
+                             max_position_embeddings=64)
+        torch.manual_seed(0)
+        model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_config(config)
+        ds_config = {
+            "train_micro_batch_size_per_gpu": 1,
+            "tensor_parallel": {
+                "autotp_size": 2
+            },
+            "zero_optimization": {
+                "stage": 0
+            },
+        }
+        engine, _, _, _ = deepspeed.initialize(model=model, config=ds_config)
+        model.eval()
+        head_dim = config.hidden_size // config.num_attention_heads
+        assert model.model.layers[0].self_attn.k_proj.weight.shape[0] == config.num_key_value_heads * head_dim // 2
+
+        device = torch.device(accelerator.current_device_name())
+        prompt_ids = torch.tensor([[5, 17, 42, 9], [33, 8, 71, 2], [64, 11, 19, 90]], device=device)
+        prompt_attn = torch.ones_like(prompt_ids)
+        new_tokens = 6
+        with torch.no_grad():
+            expected = model.generate(prompt_ids,
+                                      attention_mask=prompt_attn,
+                                      max_new_tokens=new_tokens,
+                                      do_sample=False,
+                                      eos_token_id=None,
+                                      pad_token_id=0)
+
+        rollout = HybridEngineRollout(engine,
+                                      SimpleNamespace(pad_token_id=0, eos_token_id=-1),
+                                      cfg=HybridEngineRolloutConfig(use_graph_capture=use_graph))
+        try:

+            output = rollout.generate(
+                RolloutRequest(prompt_ids, prompt_attn),
+                SamplingConfig(max_new_tokens=new_tokens, temperature=0, continuous_batch_size=2))
+            assert torch.equal(output.input_ids, expected)
+            assert model.config.num_key_value_heads == 4

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Add a distributed AutoTP rollout integration test**

Under the TP>1 scenario this fix targets, `_LocalKVModel` only mimics a shard by directly emitting `local_heads`; it never runs AutoTP, creates a TP process group, or checks parity through an actually sharded model, so regressions in the AutoTP/rollout/cache integration can still leave every new case green. Add a minimal two-rank AutoTP rollout parity case for the eager and graph paths where supported, as inference-level changes require integration rather than only synthetic unit coverage.

Added in 766d560: `TestAutoTPContinuousRollout` (`world_size = 2`) in `tests/unit/v1/test_hybrid_engine_rollout_v1.py`. It runs real AutoTP through `deepspeed.initialize` with `tensor_parallel.autotp_size=2` on a tiny Llama (4 KV heads, so each rank holds 2), and checks that the `k_proj` shards are actually split. It then runs continuous rollout with 3 requests on 2 slots, so a refill lands in an already allocated cache row. The tokens must equal `generate()` on the same sharded model, for both eager and graph capture.

Results on 2× NVIDIA H20, torch 2.9.0a0+50eac811a6.nv25.09, Transformers 4.57.6, Python 3.12.3:

| Tree | eager | graph |
| --- | --- | --- |
| this PR | pass | pass |
| rollout + static cache reverted to d8241a9 | `size of tensor a (4) must match ... b (2)` | `value tensor of shape [2, 2, 16] cannot be broadcast to ... [2, 4, 16]` |

Plain graph is not in this test, because real HF models need the mask fix in #9004 for that path; the TP2/TP2×DP4 plain-graph runs with #9004 are reported in the description. On Transformers versions whose `Cache` defines `get_query_offset` (5.x), the eager case skips until #8852 lands. The graph case still runs there. The test releases the rollout before process-group teardown because of the known NCCL graph teardown hang noted in the description.
